text:
lina: Quick sync — proposing a small refactor to the onboarding pipeline to expose prober visibility + bench sampling controls. Idea is a per-model prober config and a read-only visibility API so infra/QA can pull the latest prober status and sampled inputs. Thoughts?

ben: Sounds useful. What's the exact contract surface you want between intake and prober?

lina: Minimal: prober config (sampling rate, seed, golden flags), last-run metadata (ts, duration, pass/fail, sample id), and a link to artifacts. No model weights.

samir: Two approaches:
- A: Keep everything internal, add a fluent config that runtime picks up (fast, fewer auth changes).
- B: Surface a read-only API (/onboard/{model}/prober) so other teams can query prober state (better visibility, more work for auth + rate limits).

ash: +1 for B from observability side. Ops needs deterministic pulls for dashboards. Do we plan paginated responses for heavy artifacts? :eyes:

lina: yes pagination for artifacts. For bulk pulls we'll support rsync-like export behind a job API so we don't OOM the control plane.

ben: Performance tradeoff: adding an API means potential N*polling cost. Suggest push model via webhooks when a run completes and a read endpoint for snapshots. Push reduces load.

samir: agreed. Webhook + snapshot read endpoint. Also want a stable JSON contract so we can version it: v1 has minimal fields, v2 can add more telemetry.

ash: sample curl for read endpoint so infra can prototype quickly:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/onboard/my-model/prober_status
```
Response shape idea: {"last_run_ts":"...","status":"ok|fail","summary_url":"...","sample_id":"..."}

ben: For bench sampling we should include sampling seed in the response so QA can reproduce. Also record the seed in bench artifacts.

lina: good call. We should also restrict who can request raw samples — only roles with onboard:read:samples. Other roles get counts/metadata only.

ash: Auth note: use short-lived signed URLs for artifact downloads instead of passing data through control plane.

qa-bot: smoke-run-4943210001: prober smoke passed (samples=100, fail=0) — artifact https://s3/.../smoke-4943210001.tar.gz

ben: Regarding sampling algorithm: deterministic reservoir sampling with epoch-based seed works across restarts. Pseudocode: 
```
def pick(seed, N, k):
  rng = Random(seed)
  # reservoir sampling...
```
Include seed+epoch in metadata.

lina: KV cache/batching risk: if probes trigger runtime warmup, we might see noisy latency signals. Need to tag prober traffic so runtime can treat them as low-priority or synthetic.

samir: we can add a routing header: X-Prober-Intent: synthetic|golden|replay and have serving runtime take different cost/priority paths. That requires a small routing rule and documented behavior.

ash: rollout plan proposal: feature flag gate on per-tenant basis, enable webhooks for a small set of internal tenants, collect 2 weeks telemetry, then enable read API for broader teams.

ben: metrics to collect during canary: prober API latency, control-plane CPU/RPS, artifact download failure rate, synthetic traffic impact on tail latency.

lina: privacy note: ensure probes are sanitized — strip PII before we allow cross-team visibility. Add a required "sanitization_passed" field in metadata.

ash: ops question — how will this affect billing? If teams pull samples frequently we could get storage/egress spikes. We should rate-limit per-team and expose a quota metric.

samir: action items I can take: draft the v1 JSON contract and webhook payload, add X-Prober-Intent routing header doc, and prototype the short-lived signed URL flow.

ben: I'll own metrics + canary dashboards and a simple consumer SDK snippet for infra to use.

ash: I'll wire auth scopes (onboard:read, onboard:read:samples) and add quota policy in gateway.

lina: I'll write the short RFC blurb for the team and coordinate the canary list. Tentative schedule: RFC this week, prototype next sprint, canary after that. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
